mission_08: Anomaly detection in time series is the task of identifying unusual patterns that deviate significantly from expected behavior. These anomalies can indicate system failures, fraud, sensor malfunctions, or rare events of scientific interest. The z-score method detects point anomalies by measuring how many standard deviations each observation is from a rolling mean, flagging values that exceed a threshold. The CUSUM (Cumulative Sum) algorithm is a sequential change point detection method that accumulates deviations from the mean, making it sensitive to small persistent shifts that individual z-scores might miss. The isolation forest approach treats anomaly detection as a isolation problem: anomalies are few and different, so they can be isolated with fewer random splits than normal points. Seasonal anomaly detection accounts for periodic patterns by comparing each observation to the expected value at its seasonal position, detecting deviations that would be missed by global statistics. In this mission, you will implement all four methods, providing a comprehensive toolkit for time series anomaly detection.
